In the pairs, the 1990 and 2012/3.57 rows barely change across 1/6 s. The melt advances in slow, near-linear creep, with no acceleration or settle.
The 2012 bar is the only thing animating in the chart hold. The rest of the 48 bars sit static for several seconds (dead air).

The end frame has a lot of small right-aligned type, plus the source line, the Greenland silhouette and the headline, all fighting in the bottom-right corner. The Greenland shape is undersized for the payoff.
gaps: Pacing: 3 shots across 30 s, with 12–13 s holds where the only motion is a slow, uniform dissolve of ice. Top work would cut or re-frame every ~2–3 s, adding pushes, scale shifts and break-ups with real anticipation and settle so the collapse feels physical (calving, drift, weight) rather than a mask wipe.

Arc and transitions: per-second change is flat apart from three spikes at the cuts. There is no build into the 2012 record or release after it. The cut from ice to chart is a hard swap; a match-transform would be stronger, with the ice slabs becoming the bars and the 3.57 stencil becoming the orange bar, then back to the map.

Sound: a dense harmonic drone bed with three broadband hits that line up with the cuts at ~4.4 s, 13.1 s and 17.8 s, plus a noise swell at ~25 s. Beyond that it is static, with no cracking or ice foley tied to individual breaks and little dynamic shaping. The record moment and the Greenland reveal get no distinct sonic peak or silence for release.
